tagline: A road laid on a copper railbed, across the delta.
intro: The highway begins at the ferry dock in Cordova, a town no road connects to the rest of Alaska. It runs out past Eyak Lake and the airport and onto the old grade of the Copper River and Northwestern Railway, which from 1911 to 1938 brought copper ore down from Kennecott to the harbor. The pavement lasts 12 miles. After that it is gravel, heading east and northeast over several sloughs through the Chugach National Forest.
Work on the road began in 1945, meant to reach Chitina and the state highways. The Good Friday earthquake of 1964 stopped it, and it never got there.

moments.title: Cordova
moments.text: Laid out in 1906 as the railroad's terminus, the town was ablaze with flags when President Harding called in 1923, and he rode through it in the only transportation available, an Army truck.

moments.title: Copper River Delta
moments.text: 584 square miles of delta, part of the Western Hemisphere Shorebird Reserve Network, where more than 500,000 migratory birds stop over or make their home.

moments.title: Million Dollar Bridge
moments.text: Raised in 1909 and 1910 between the Childs and Miles glaciers, built to stand up to icebergs 20 feet high riding a seven-mile-an-hour current.

practical: Only the first 12 miles are paved. The rest of the highway is gravel.
